It says: "عند دلك جسم نٌ عازل نٌ ببعضهما البعض , ماذا تكون شحنة كل منهما ؟" Means: "When two insulating bodies are brought together, what is the charge of each of them?" So two insulating bodies brought together. The question likely about electrostatic induction? Actually if two insulating bodies are brought together, they can exchange charge? If they are insulated, they don't conduct, so no charge transfer. So each remains neutral? But maybe they become charged? Let's parse options:

A. شٌحنان بشحنت نٌ مختلفت نٌ ومتساو تٌ نٌ
Probably means: "Two charges with different charges and equal magnitude"? Hard.

B. ظٌلان متعادل نٌ و لا شٌحنان
Probably: "Two neutral bodies and no charge".

C. شٌحنان بشحنت نٌ سالبت نٌ متساو تٌ نٌ
Probably: "Two charges with equal negative charge".

D. شٌحنان بشحنت نٌ موجبت نٌ متساو تٌ نٌ
Probably: "Two charges with equal positive charge".

The correct answer: If two insulating bodies are brought together, they remain neutral, no charge transfer. So B: "Two neutral bodies and no charge". So answer letter B.
